title: The day Sri left heaven
hook: a trampled garland, and the goddess Sri walks out of heaven
carry: sri is her gift, and pride drives it away
tomorrow: a sage swims a flood and finds the world inside a child. how?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra in worship: greet every guardian on the way to the center. Today, the first word of its name, and the day it went missing.

The sage Durvasa, famous for his temper, is given a garland of heavenly flowers, and he offers it to Indra, king of the gods. Indra, riding high on his elephant, tosses the garland onto the elephant's head. The elephant pulls it off and tramples it into the dirt. Durvasa curses him: your fortune will leave you. And she does. In the Vishnu Purana's telling, Sri herself walks out of the three worlds. The plants wither, the offerings stop, the gods lose their shine, and the demons drive them out. Everything Indra had came from her, and he hadn't noticed until she was gone. She returns only much later, rising from the churned ocean on a lotus.
screen: `A GARLAND, TRAMPLED.` → `SRI WALKS OUT.` → `THE GODS LOSE THEIR SHINE.`

segments.voice: Sri, also spelled Shri, means radiance, beauty, good fortune, the sense of things going well, and it's a name of the Goddess Lakshmi. Notice the teaching in the story: Indra thought his shine was his own. It wasn't. Sri is the Goddess's gift, and pride drives her away. That's why, in many Hindu families, Shri is written at the very top of a wedding card, a letter or a new account book, before the first real line. It's a small act of humility: the blessing is hers, and it goes first, before my effort. Shri is set before the names of gods, holy places and honored people too. And it's the first word of the Sri Yantra: the yantra of Sri, the diagram of the auspicious one. The Lalita Sahasranama opens the same way. Her first name is Srimata, the auspicious mother; the next, Sri Maharajni, the great queen. Before the hymn says anything else about her, it says the word for radiance and blessing. The square, the lotuses, the triangles and the point all sit inside one short word: the same one families write before anything else.
screen: `SRI: RADIANCE AND GOOD FORTUNE.` · `HER GIFT; PRIDE DRIVES HER AWAY.` · `SHRI GOES FIRST: A BLESSING, NOT A BOAST.` · `HER NAMES OPEN WITH SRI.` · then, large: `SRI IS HER GIFT. PRIDE DRIVES IT AWAY.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and a piece of paper, and at the very top write one word you'd want to go first, before anything else on the page: Shri, if it's part of your family's way, or another word that means blessing to you. Write it slowly. Then sit with the page in front of you and let that one word be all that's on it for a while.
The Sri Yantra: the yantra of Sri, radiance and blessing, the word Lalita's names begin with.
For the road: Sri is her gift, and pride drives it away. Indra forgot; that's why Shri goes first on the page. That's the day.
